title: AN EMPIRICAL STUDY OF METRICS TO MEASURE REPRESENTATIONAL HARMS IN PRE-TRAINED LANGUAGE MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the language modeling likelihood (perplexity or pseudo-perplexity) of implicitly harmful versus benign statements targeting racial and ethnic groups (e.g., African American, Asian, Chinese, Mexican, Latinx, Native-American, Middle-Eastern) using a subset of the ToxiGen dataset, and calculating a safety score using a Mann-Whitney U-test.

Measuring the language modeling likelihood of implicitly harmful versus benign statements about women, calculating a safety score based on scaled perplexity, and correlating these results with existing gender stereotyping metrics like Regard, Causal Mediation Analysis (CMA), and StereoSet.

Measuring the language modeling likelihood of implicitly harmful versus benign statements targeting religious groups (Jewish, Muslim) using the ToxiGen dataset to calculate a representational harm safety score.
Calculating the scaled perplexity and safety score of implicitly harmful versus benign statements targeting the LGBTQ demographic to quantify representational harms.
Measuring the language model's propensity to generate implicitly harmful versus benign statements regarding physically and mentally disabled individuals using perplexity and Mann-Whitney U-tests.
